To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of contextual information and user embeddings in addition to content-driven modeling improves the classification performance on the sarcasm detection task.

(a) context-based feature extractors, such as CNNs and RNNs, are more effective in detecting sarcasm than content-based feature extractions, and (b) the combination of content and context-based feature extractions further boosts the classification performance.

(i) context and user embeddings are useful features for sarcasm detection; (ii) the performance of a sarcasm detector can be significantly improved by using both content and contextual features; (iii) a sarcasm classifier can be built using the proposed hybrid model that achieves a performance that is comparable to that of human annotators.
